content: Individuals, caregivers, families, and communities are intentionally included as active participants and beneficiaries within trusted healthcare systems. These systems are designed to address their specific needs and preferences in a manner that is compassionate and holistic. People-centered care also emphasizes the importance of providing individuals with the necessary education and support to make informed decisions and actively engage in their own healthcare. This approach prioritizes the health needs and expectations of individuals rather than focusing solely on diseases. Rehabilitation refers to a collection of interventions aimed at optimizing an individual’s functional abilities and minimizing disability in the context of their health conditions and environmental interactions. The term health condition encompasses diseases (both acute and chronic), disorders, injuries, or trauma. It may also include other circumstances such as pregnancy, aging, stress, congenital anomalies, or genetic predispositions. Rehabilitation outcomes are defined as measurable changes in an individual’s functional status over time that can be directly attributed to rehabilitation interventions. These outcomes may include improvements in daily living activities (e.g., home care, school, work) and enhanced quality of life. Universal health coverage is defined as ensuring that all individuals have access to the promotive, preventive, curative, rehabilitative, and palliative health services they require. These services must be of sufficient quality to be effective, while also ensuring that their utilization does not result in financial hardship for the user.
